factProposals.value: Confirmation emails are sent through the Gmail API using an OAuth refresh token read from environment variables.
A confirmation can only be sent for a booking the owner has approved.
Each sent confirmation is logged with a booking id and timestamp; the audit log does not store the customer's email address.

decisions.statement: A send that times out or drops the connection is not retried; only 429/5xx answers from Gmail are retried, up to 2 times.
decisions.rationale: Gmail may have accepted the message, and a retry could email the customer twice.

decisions.statement: A booking is marked sent before the audit entry is written, and a failed log write is retried on the next call.
decisions.rationale: A logging failure must never cause a second email.

limitations.statement: The Gmail adapter has only been tested against a fake HTTP layer; no real email has been sent because no Gmail credentials were available.
There is no database: booking status is held in memory and lost on restart; only the audit log is persisted.
An ambiguous send failure (timeout) is shown as an error even if Gmail delivered the email.
